summary: Backend-only testing of Iter 133 Moteur D (signalmar.v4) bug fix. PRIMARY BUG FIX VERIFIED: Vilaine route (engine_d) returns HTTP 200 with shallow_route=true, wrong_side_marks empty, and no 'MAUVAIS CÔTÉ' warnings — the SIDE_RULES_OPEN leak in _run_shallow/_last_resort no longer strips reliable lateral sides under ISOLATED_SIDE_BATHY. Engines listing correct (engine_d=signalmar.v4, engine_b=signalmar.v2, engine_a=signalmar.v1, engine_c=signalmar.v3). Non-regression Moteur B: HTTP 200 and wrong_side_marks field absent (audit is D-only) — OK. Full pytest suite tests/test_iter133_sens_conventionnel_isolees.py = 9/9 PASSED. HOWEVER: the Illur reference case via HTTP with the exact body from the review request (no lateral_margin_m) FAILS — the route passes SOUTH of Illur at ~91 m (closest waypoint lat=47.5798 < 47.5827), and the audit correctly populates wrong_side_marks=[Illur]. Verified locally: forcing lateral_margin_m=50 makes the same HTTP route pass NORTH (audit empty). Root cause: with the HTTP default AUTO_LATERAL_M=10 m the A* squeezes through the ~90 m gap on the wrong side of Illur — the ISOLATED_SIDE_BATHY rasterize block extends only 200 m on shallow cells (per algo comment), and the shallow SW cell next to Illur is not covered strongly enough at 10 m margin. So the fix works correctly in shallow/last_resort mode (primary Vilaine bug) and with wider lateral margins (unit test uses 50 m), but the DEFAULT HTTP call with tight margin still routes SOUTH of Illur — the audit warns the user but does not re-route.

minor.endpoint: POST /api/routes/compute {engine_id:'engine_d', Illur ref case, no lateral_margin_m}
minor.issue: Route passes SOUTH of Illur (closest waypoint lat=47.579788 vs Illur lat=47.5827118). wrong_side_marks correctly reports Illur at 91.4 m 'à tribord' (audit works). With explicit lateral_margin_m=50 the same HTTP call passes NORTH (audit empty). The unit test test_moteur_d_passe_au_nord_d_illur_dans_les_deux_sens passes because it calls SignalmarV4.compute_auto directly with lateral_margin_m=50, but the HTTP default (AUTO_LATERAL_M=10) squeezes through the wrong side. Fix candidates: (a) widen ISOLATED_SIDE_BATHY rasterize block on the danger cells of isolated laterals so it holds even with tight margins; (b) raise AUTO_LATERAL_M plancher for signalmar.v4 engines; (c) after A* succeeds, if wrong_side_marks is non-empty for a reliable-direction lateral, retry once with an increased lateral margin. Reference: /app/backend/routers/routing.py:121 (AUTO_LATERAL_M=10.0) and /app/backend/core/routing_engines/algos/signalmar_v4/__init__.py:48 (_INFLUENCE_M=200).

rca_of_issue: Primary Vilaine bug (No1 laissée du mauvais côté à 9,8 m): root cause was SIDE_RULES_OPEN in routing.py _run_shallow/_last_resort lifting ALL lateral side constraints in seamarks.rasterize_blocked. Fix (verified working): under ISOLATED_SIDE_BATHY (armed only by signalmar.v4), rasterize_blocked keeps reliable-direction lateral blocks even when SIDE_RULES_OPEN is set. Vilaine HTTP call now returns shallow_route=true with empty wrong_side_marks and no 'MAUVAIS CÔTÉ' warnings — bug resolved. Residual Illur case: the fix hinges on the shallow-side rasterize extending far enough from the lateral to force the A* around it; with AUTO_LATERAL_M=10 m and a ~200 m influence radius, the A* can still find a path on the wrong side of Illur through a locally deep 'tongue'. This isn't the SIDE_RULES_OPEN regression that was fixed — it's a distinct pre-existing limitation exposed by the review request's exact HTTP body.
